detailed_analysis: The spectrum is an essentially textbook anatase TiO2 Raman fingerprint. Consolidating the 10 fitted components into physically meaningful bands: (1) the dominant band at ~140 cm-1 (fitted as overlapping components at 136 and 142, combined the strongest feature) is the anatase Eg mode (literature 144 cm-1); (2) a very weak feature near 201 cm-1 corresponds to the weak anatase Eg mode (~197 cm-1, often near detection limit); (3) the ~395 cm-1 band (components 382+395) is the B1g mode (~399 cm-1); (4) the ~515 cm-1 band (components 513+532) is the overlapping A1g + B1g pair (~513+519 cm-1); (5) the ~636 cm-1 band is the Eg mode (~639 cm-1); (6) the weak broad ~795 cm-1 feature is a known anatase overtone/combination band. This five-mode pattern (144 strong, 197 weak, 399, 519, 639) matches anatase within a few cm-1 in BOTH position AND relative intensity (Eg 144 dominant), satisfying the multi-band matching requirement. No band matches rutile (which requires 447/612 and lacks the strong 144), and there is no carbonate/sulfate/silicate/phosphate primary band. The strong dominant low-frequency band decisively separates anatase from rutile. Residual analysis: the coherent oscillatory residuals at the apices of the 140, 395, and 515 bands (up to +/-10-15 sigma) indicate the pseudo-Voigt cores under-fit the true, sharper Lorentzian peak shapes of a well-crystallized phase; these are shape artifacts, not evidence of additional phases. The chemistry is pattern-only (no EDX/XRF provided), but the pattern completeness is high. No parameter uncertainties were reported (all *_err null), so peak positions/widths cannot be given formal error bars; the assignment rests on pattern matching, which is robust here.

scientific_claims.claim: The unknown compound is anatase-phase TiO2, identified from its Raman bands at ~140 (Eg, dominant), ~197 (Eg, weak), ~395 (B1g), ~515 (A1g+B1g), and ~639 cm-1 (Eg), matching anatase in position and relative intensity within a few cm-1; no uncertainties reported.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Unambiguous phase identification (anatase vs rutile vs brookite) is critical for photocatalysis, pigments, and battery/sensor applications where anatase's specific band structure governs activity; the dominant 144 cm-1 Eg mode cleanly excludes rutile.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone confirmed that a Raman spectrum with a dominant ~144 cm-1 Eg band plus 197/399/519/639 cm-1 modes uniquely identifies anatase-phase TiO2 relative to rutile and brookite?

model_type: Sum of 10 pseudo-Voigt peaks on light ALS-corrected baseline (raw-space fit = peaks + ALS baseline)

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt peaks on a near-zero ALS-corrected baseline, as proposed, BUT allow the ~305 cm⁻¹ feature to be modeled with up to two components (e.g. seeds ~298 and ~310 cm⁻¹) to reproduce its flat-topped/bimodal profile. Start with the single 305 component; if the baseline-corrected residual there shows a bimodal (two-hump) signature above ~3× noise, retain the second component. Model becomes 7 (or 8) pseudo-Voigt peaks; the 395, 515, 638, 140, 195, 793 bands remain single symmetric pseudo-Voigt as they appear clean/symmetric in the full plot and zooms.

issues.problem: The dominant peak is poorly modeled: the fit is too narrow at the top and too broad in the wings, and the data appears asymmetric relative to the single symmetric pseudo-Voigt.
The ~394 peak is under-resolved: the fit systematically misses the leading edge/shoulder around x≈370-380 and the peak apex, producing a coherent oscillation.
Systematic oscillatory residual around the 514 peak indicating shape/width mismatch.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Re-seed/optimize the main peaks (fix peak_1 shape/width, add or re-seed a shoulder near x≈372, re-tune peak_6 near x≈538) and reinitialize the collapsed peak_2 to fit the real feature near x≈197.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt peaks on a near-zero ALS-corrected baseline. The 305 cm⁻¹ feature may be modeled with up to two components (seeds ~298 and ~310 cm⁻¹) to reproduce its flat-topped/bimodal profile, retaining the second only if the baseline-corrected residual there is bimodal above ~3× noise. The model remains within the plan-locked family of symmetric pseudo-Voigt peaks (with the allowed 305-region second component and the asymmetric-profile fallback for dispersive S-shape residuals). Concrete band assignments incorporating verification feedback: (1) The dominant ~141 cm⁻¹ band is re-seeded for center/width with eta free to balance a Lorentzian wing / Gaussian core mismatch; because its rising flank is asymmetric, a permitted shoulder component is seeded near x≈130 to capture the asymmetric rising flank/cusp — this uses the plan's existing shoulder-on-bimodal/asymmetry rule rather than adding a new model type. (2) The collapsed peak_2 near ~197 cm⁻¹ (previously amplitude~0.018, eta~0, relative intensity ~5e-8) is reinitialized with a physically meaningful amplitude/FWHM to fit the small real bump near x≈197 instead of parking on noise. (3) The ~394 cm⁻¹ band gains a permitted shoulder component seeded near x≈372 to capture the under-resolved low-x leading edge, or alternatively its width/eta are re-optimized if a single component clears the residual criterion. (4) The ~514 cm⁻¹ band width/eta are re-tuned, with a shoulder component near x≈538 considered only if the oscillatory residual remains bimodal above threshold. The 515, 638, 195, 793 bands otherwise remain single symmetric pseudo-Voigt unless their zoomed residuals demand a permitted shoulder/asymmetric switch.

issues.problem: Low-amplitude oscillatory residuals (~2-3% of local signal) on the tallest peaks produce large σ-multiples
